source.title: Deep Learning is Robust to Massive Label Noise
source.authors: D. Rolnick; Andreas Veit; Serge J. Belongie; N. Shavit

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests generalization under massive label noise in image classification, using added noisy examples alongside a fixed set of clean examples. This is a related setting to the claim versions but does not reproduce their random-labeling or training-error measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy after training with added noisy examples. It does not report training error, fitting of completely random labels, training time, or fitting shuffled pixels. White-noise inputs are added as noisy examples; the outcome is test accuracy, not whether the network fits those inputs.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's test-performance component in a different noise setting: it increases the randomly labeled fraction by adding examples while preserving the clean-example count. Test accuracy declines while substantial generalization remains. It does not establish perfect training fit or memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that networks can generalize under massive non-adversarial label noise given enough clean examples, with the required clean-example count increasing slightly faster than the noisy-to-clean ratio. They also conclude that noise reduces effective batch size and that larger batches and lower learning rates can mitigate its effects.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard AdaDelta training on datasets diluted by adding noisy examples for each clean example; it does not use the original studies’ intervention of completely randomizing the training labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, noise source and structure, clean training-set size, batch size, and learning rate affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding randomly labeled white-noise inputs does not appreciably reduce CIFAR-10 test accuracy; CIFAR-100 distractors cause roughly half the decline caused by CIFAR-10 distractors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of noisy additional examples on generalization depends on their input distribution. These results do not measure fitting unstructured inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher batch sizes improve noise robustness, lower learning rates become preferable as noise increases, and an infinite-batch surrogate loss yields essentially unchanged test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise reduces the effective batch size, making generalization depend on batch size and learning rate. These measurements do not establish the time required to memorize random labels.

record.problems: The reported main outcomes are test accuracy; training error is not reported. Several result values are conveyed in figures, and the paper selects the learning rate giving the best performance for each noise level.
record.rows_left_out: No results meet the row criteria for the listed versions: test accuracy under added label noise does not establish fitting of random labels or the training-fit component of V4. The paper also cites Zhang et al. (2017) for fitting random inputs; that cited result is not this study’s result.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without hyperparameter changes.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Zero training error on shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit and memorization of noisy labels; the fully random endpoint; degradation when increasing corruption removes clean examples from a fixed-size dataset. Learning rates are selected separately for each noise level.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

missing.what: Rows for V4's test-performance component: test accuracy across uniform-noise levels for each architecture and dataset. The record declares these outcomes excluded, but its exclusion incorrectly requires training-fit measurements before recording the separately tested test-performance component.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its preserved clean-example count and separately selected learning rates prevent treating its high-noise accuracy as a challenge to chance performance under completely random labeling. Repeated images can receive conflicting labels, so these experiments also cannot be assumed to permit perfect training fit.

versions.untested_parts: Does not assign completely random labels to the entire training set and report training error or test error at chance.
Does not compare training time for noisy and true labels or report convergence slowdown as label corruption rises.
Does not report training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Varies the amount of added noise and reports test accuracy, but does not report perfect training fit or test error rising steadily toward chance as labels are corrupted from none to all.
Does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
Does not measure the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned.

relationships.condition: Uniform random label noise added to a fixed clean dataset, with finite batches and learning-rate selection at each noise level.
relationships.reason: Text and Figures 1–3 show declining test accuracy with increasing noise while real signal remains learnable: MNIST ConvNet accuracy is 91% at 100:1 noise, CIFAR-10 ResNet approximately 85% at 10:1, and ImageNet approximately 70% top-5 at 5:1. This supports only the test-performance component; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy declined with added noise but remained 91% for the MNIST ConvNet at 100:1 noise, approximately 85% for CIFAR-10 ResNet at 10:1, and approximately 70% top-5 on ImageNet at 5:1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
